question.problem:
Which of the following are elementary matrices?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An elementary matrix is a matrix obtained from the identity matrix by applying exactly one elementary row operation. 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- The matrix $T$ is not an elementary matrix because it can't be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying only one elementary row operation.

- The matrix $U$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=9{R}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}:=9{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

- The matrix $X$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =X\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only $U$ and $X$ are elementary matrices.
